title: Extend nth-root irrationality to algebraic irrationality via irreducible polynomials

problemStatement.formal: For prime p and n ≥ 2, X^n - p is irreducible over ℚ (Eisenstein + Gauss), hence p^(1/n) is irrational. More generally, any root of an irreducible polynomial of degree ≥ 2 over ℚ is irrational.
problemStatement.plain: Prove irrationality of nth roots of primes via irreducible polynomials (Eisenstein criterion + Gauss lemma), subsuming the counting-argument approach.
whyMatters: Provides a more structural approach to irrationality than ad-hoc counting arguments
Eisenstein criterion + Gauss lemma is a fundamental technique in algebraic number theory
Connects irrationality to the broader theory of minimal polynomials and algebraic degrees

proven: irreducible_no_rational_root: irreducible p ∈ ℚ[X] with deg ≥ 2 has no rational root
irrational_root_of_irreducible: real roots of such p are irrational
X_pow_sub_prime_irreducible_int: X^n - p irreducible over ℤ (Eisenstein at (p))
eisenstein_X_pow_sub_prime: X^n - p irreducible over ℚ (Gauss lemma transfer)
irrational_nthRoot_of_prime: p^(1/n) irrational for prime p, n ≥ 2

insights: Eisenstein criterion API: Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion requires 6 goals: prime ideal, leading coeff not in P, lower coeffs in P, positive degree, constant coeff not in P², isPrimitive
Gauss lemma: IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast transfers irreducibility ℤ→ℚ; use convert+ext+simp for coefficient matching

leadingCoeff_X_pow_sub_C and degree_X_pow_sub_C take (0 < n), while monic_X_pow_sub_C takes (n ≠ 0)
